page: Amazon Web Services m6g.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64), this instance features 2 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The underlying hardware includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per processor. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the m6g.large delivers moderate single-core capabilities but exhibits limitations under multi-core and memory-intensive workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance falls within the average range, whereas multi-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor throughput, with read-only large block transfers registering at 36.2 GB/sec and write operations at 18.38 GB/sec. Similarly, database and web serving benchmarks, such as Redis SET operations at 2.29 million operations per second and static web serving at 2.35 GB/sec, place the instance in the lower performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides a lower-cost alternative to traditional x86 instances for workloads that do not require high-performance computing or advanced vector instructions like AVX. However, tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage and poor multi-threaded scaling, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1730.0. The instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, including basic web serving, small database operations, and simple text or image processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.large is a general-purpose instance powered by a 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor with 2 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture. It features 8.0 GB of system memory, a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and relies entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark data indicates average single-core CPU performance, but weak multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities, with Geekbench multi-core scores and Redis operations falling into the lower percentiles. The instance lacks advanced x86 instruction sets like AVX but includes hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. Qualitatively, the m6g.large offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM-native development and low-intensity workloads. It is best suited for basic web serving, lightweight database operations, and simple application hosting where high multi-threaded performance is not required.
